Time: 3 min. Teaching intent: Retrieve prior knowledge before revealing the method.
Talk track: Does this predict package warpage by itself?
Expected answer / misconception: No. Constraint, layer geometry, and stiffness determine the assembled response.
Visual: The three conditions identify what must be compared.
[Sources]
R7: IEEE TCPMT, Thermomechanical Challenges of 2.5-D Packaging | https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10256204

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: A coefficient of thermal expansion links temperature change to free thermal strain over a stated range. Trace the visual in order: temperature change; CTE; free strain. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: Synthetic arithmetic: 10 ppm/K over 100 K gives 0.001 free strain if the coefficient is constant.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.
[Sources]
R7: IEEE TCPMT, Thermomechanical Challenges of 2.5-D Packaging | https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10256204
R8: IEEE TCPMT, Simulation and Experimental Study of Fan-Out Warpage | https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/8590768

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Work the example step by step.
Talk track: Set up the case: Synthetic arithmetic: 10 ppm/K over 100 K gives 0.001 free strain if the coefficient is constant. Identify the starting information, state the reasoning step aloud, then ask what observation would check the conclusion. Stop before the next slide's question is answered.
Expected answer / misconception: Students must identify the input, the inference, and the check. 
Visual: Three-part reasoning path separates the example from its verification.
